question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is **"lend."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Lend"** means to give something to someone for a temporary period of time, expecting it to be returned. (थोड़े समय के लिए उधार देना)

 
 
• **Example:** *Could you **lend__** me Rs 100 until Friday?*
 
 
 
• It is the correct option to fill in the blank because the sentence is talking about someone giving something to someone else.
 
• The grammatical point to note is that** "lend**" is the present tense form of the verb, while **"lent"** is the past tense form.
 
• Other forms of the word include** "lender" (a person or organization that lends money)** and **"loan" (the act of lending something)**.
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
• Correct passage*:*

Dill ate, and ate and ate. He hadn’t eaten __since__ last night. He used all his money for a ticket, __boarded__ the train, as he had done many times, coolly chatted with the conductor, to __whom__ Dill was a familiar sight, but he had not the nerve to invoke the rule on small children travelling a distance alone; if you’ve lost your money the conductor will __**lend**__ you enough for dinner and your father will ______ (5) ______ him back at the end of the line. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Borrow" **is the opposite of **"lend"** and means to take something from someone else temporarily. (उधार, कर्ज़ या ऋण लेना)
 
• **"Take"** is similar to **"borrow"** but does not necessarily imply that the item will be returned.
